newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: U.N. chief hopeful on Mobutu's return to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief hopeful on Mobutu's return to Zaire.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan welcomed Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's return home, saying he hoped Mobutu would push for dialogue to end the war tearing his country apart.
"I hope now that he is back he will begin to take some initiatives and provide some leadership," Annan said at the start of talks with the Namibian government in Windhoek.
"His absence created a political vacuum which made it difficult for one to interact with the Zairean side," he told reporters.
Mobutu flew home on Friday from the French Riviera, where he had been convalescing from prostate cancer surgery last year.
Annan, visiting Africa for the first time as head of the United Nations, was optimistic that a summit scheduled in Lome, Togo, on March 26 would lead Zaire towards peace.

"I hope that soon after Lome and with the involvement of the governments in the region, and now that Mobutu is also back in the country, we will be able to get serious talks going and get a ceasefire on the ground," he said.
"But as we work on this, we are going to need the support and cooperation and the persistent pressure of all the leaders in the region on the protagonists."
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has said he would prefer to see talks initiated prior to a ceasefire, but Annan disagreed with this approach saying:
"I think at this stage we may have to proceed simultaneously with talks and a ceasefire."

Annan was on a brief stopover in Namibia en route to Angola, where he will push for progress with the delayed installation of a government of national unity to formally end 19 years of civil war between the MPLA-led government and UNITA movement.
